records.title: Radar chart with lines only
records.sees: Drawn filled, and the axis labels can collide and clip at the right edge. Each series also carries an area fill beside its line, and Keynote fills the marker radar as well, so that fill is the likely cause; cause not confirmed
records.workaround: Not tested: variants with the area fill set to no fill look the same in PowerPoint and have not been opened in Keynote
records.note: In Keynote 15.4 a series area set to no fill (a:noFill) drew the radar unfilled (#1416 item 1); OPF 0.36.0 does not write it, and Keynote 16.0 still fills the radar (coverage-charts 5).

records.title: Area chart with a gap in the data
records.sees: The gap is bridged by the area (PowerPoint shows the gap)

records.title: Secondary value axis
records.sees: Only its 0% and 40% labels, and the legend overlaps them (PowerPoint shows 0% to 40% in steps of 10%); cause not confirmed
records.workaround: Not tested: variants without the major unit and with the General number format have not been opened in Keynote
records.note: Finding QC-02 (Keynote 16.0, OPF 0.36.0) narrows the cause: Keynote rewrites a value-axis step that does not divide the range (46/20 becomes 23, 250/100 becomes 83.3) and a percent axis keeps only 0% and its maximum; even steps are kept. It shows on any value axis with such a step, not only a secondary one. In Keynote 15.4, leaving out c:majorUnit restored the labels (#1416 item 2); not re-run on 16.0.

records.title: Reference line
records.sees: The line is drawn at the right value; its label is not (the legend names it). On one bar chart the label collided with a bar value, because Keynote lays the bars out on the tick marks
records.workaround: Name the line; do not rely on the label
records.note: Keynote 16.0 with OPF 0.36.0: the label is still dropped; the collision with a bar value is gone on coverage-charts 16, inferred only because the highlight form (MX-03) moves the bars.

records.title: Fonts the Mac lacks (Aptos without Office)
records.sees: Helvetica, which is wider: long titles gain a line over the content, side-by-side text touches, table headers break mid-word, bullet dots are smaller; the Warnings window names the missing fonts
records.workaround: Export with `--typefaces safe` (it removes the warning; whether it removes the overlaps is not yet measured), or install the fonts on the Mac. A Keynote export profile is planned (OpenPresentation/opf#1298)
warning: The font Aptos is missing. Your text might look different.
The font Aptos Display is missing. Your text might look different.
records.note: Aptos and Aptos Display are the default theme's fonts; on a Mac without Office Keynote draws Latin text in Helvetica and Helvetica Bold. Findings LY-01, LY-02, LG-01, SW-01, MX-07, MX-08, RT-06 and QT-01 are its effects (59 of the round's 100 wrong slides). A font the deck chose itself is named the same way (Roboto, Roboto Mono, Open Sans, Noto Naskh Arabic in the round). --typefaces safe removed the banner and the lines in the round's font test. The first round (Keynote 15.1.1, OPF 0.34.0) recorded the effect in the quote row.
